e.markdown:
**Diagnosis**: At T+2 min the collision probability on TM-CONJ-02 reads 0.00021 (Pc = 2.1 e-4) [TM-CONJ-02], exceeding the 1 e-4 action threshold reported in the conjunction message CDM-0412 [CDM-0412]. The FDIR event FE-201 flagged this as a critical conjunction-screen violation. The thrusters that would perform the avoidance burn are the 1 N monopropellant units P-PROP-04, whose catalyst-bed heater suffers from NCR-002 [NCR-002].

**Why the build record mattered**: The spec requirement REQ-PROP-028 calls for the catalyst bed to reach 315 °C in 30 min preheat. NCR-002 shows the as-flown heater resistance (52 Ω vs 46 ± 2 Ω) limits the bed to 290 °C after 30 min, meaning the thruster needs about 43.4 min to reach 315 °C (flight impact: “Every burn needs about 13 min more preheat than the spec allows”) [NCR-002, asFlown: “Use-as-is under deviation”]. Consequently, the policy moved the decision deadline from the spec-based T+45 min to T+32 min to ensure preheat can finish before the operator-available window, a shift of ~13 min driven solely by the build record.

**Public precedent**: WEB-1 notes that reducing catalytic-bed dimensions cut transient preheat time from 15 min to 52 s in a monopropellant thruster study [WEB-1]. WEB-2 describes preheating characteristics of a hydrogen-peroxide monopropellant thruster with manganese-oxide catalyst, reporting that optimum preheat temperature was investigated [WEB-2].

**For the operator**:
- **At the next pass (Svalbard, T+38 min)**  
  • Confirm that preheat for P-PROP-04 began by the T+32 min deadline and monitor temperature telemetry.  
  • Verify that the collision-avoidance burn command was uplinked and check burn start time and duration.  
  • Re-examine TM-CONJ-02 after the burn to ensure Pc falls below the 1 e-4 threshold.  
- **Afterwards**  
  • Around T+50 min (post-burn), validate that the executed Δv matches the planned 0.075 m/s and that the remaining budget is 130.93 m/s (source REQ-SYS-002).  
  • At the McMurdo pass (T+133 min), perform a full health check of P-PROP-04 (thruster status, heater telemetry) and log any anomalies for incorporation into the next build’s NCR.
